subject: Close sprint: evaluation plan and GPU tradeoffs for DataPulse
messages:
From: Lucas Martin <lucas.martin@datapulse.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluation & MAP request — hardware tradeoffs + timeline

Tessa / Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we discussed with our infra and procurement teams, we need a concise mutual action plan and an evaluation matrix that will let us validate latency/throughput and identify the right GPU fleet shape for our production footprint. High level asks:

- Clear MAP with milestones and decision gates to close by end of Q3.
- Evaluation targets: TTFT (time-to-first-token), p50/p95 latency for 512/2048 tokens, throughput at 1k and 10k concurrent requests, and recommended concurrency profiles.
- Comparison across A100 / H100 / L40S, and guidance on MIG vs full-GPU for our expected mix.

Can you share a MAP + benchmarking template and a proposed sprint/timeline? Procurement would like a sense of cost tradeoffs correlated to performance so we can size reserved capacity.

Lucas
Infrastructure Lead, DataPulse

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Lucas Martin <lucas.martin@datapulse.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation & MAP request — hardware tradeoffs + timeline

Lucas — thanks for the clear asks. Attaching a first-draft MAP and a benchmarking template to get us started (DP_MAP_v1.xlsx, benchmark-template.csv). Key notes up front:

1) Proposed evaluation sprint (2 weeks):
   - Week 1: reproducible baseline runs (A100, H100, L40S) with standard prompt sets (512/2048 tokens). Measure TTFT, p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec and memory footprint.
   - Week 2: concurrency stress (ramped to target concurrency), MIG slicing tests (1/2/4 slices per GPU where applicable), and cost-per-token modeling.

2) Bench targets and pass/fail gates:
   - TTFT target: <= 60 ms for short prompts (512 tokens) at p50; p95 <= 120 ms on dedicated capacity for chat gen use-case.
   - Throughput: baseline tokens/sec per GPU and aggregate throughput at 1k and 10k concurrent simulated users.
   - Concurrency: test 8, 32, 128 simultaneous requesters; note degradation curves and tail latencies.

3) Hardware matrix we will evaluate: A100 80GB (full), H100 80GB (full), L40S 48GB (full), plus MIG-config variants where supported (A100 MIG 7g/14g slices, H100 MIG equivalents; L40S has limited MIG).

4) Output deliverables:
   - CSV with raw logs + a summarized KPI sheet (p50/p95/TTFT/throughput/cost).
   - Recommendation: fleet sizing for steady-state and burst (capacity units by GPU type).
   - MAP milestones: evaluation complete, procurement review, pricing lock, pilot deployment, production cutover.

Action: if this aligns, we’ll schedule a short kickoff tomorrow to lock dataset and stable model version. Looking to close contract terms within 4 weeks after evaluation if results match the targets.

Attachments: DP_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP draft), benchmark-template.csv (run template)

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation & MAP request — hardware tradeoffs + timeline

Tessa / team — quick operational notes before the kickoff:

- Test harness: I’ll provision the workload generator and shared S3 buckets for logs. The benchmark-template.csv includes the canonical prompt list (50 short, 30 long, 20 burst scenarios).
- Dataset & model: ask DataPulse to confirm the model checkpoint/version they want pinned (we recommend a stable open checkpoint).
- MIG details: when we run MIG on A100/H100 we should test both 7g and 14g slices (A100 80GB supports up to 7g slices usually). L40S: confirm if they want any MIG — most customers get better mid-range density with full L40S instances for throughput workloads.
- Measurement hooks: include token-level timestamps and per-request KV-cache hit metrics so we can attribute TTFT regression to cache warming vs model compute.

(Quote from Tessa's mail)
> 1) Proposed evaluation sprint (2 weeks):
>    - Week 1: reproducible baseline runs (A100, H100, L40S) with standard prompt sets (512/2048 tokens). Measure TTFT, p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec and memory footprint.

I’ll prepare the runbook and a short checklist for the kickoff. Karthik — can you validate the run parameters and MIG config matrix?

Thanks,
Monica
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lucas Martin <lucas.martin@datapulse.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Preliminary benchmark notes — baseline 1TB dataset, model v3.1

Lucas — ran the baseline suite this week across three flavors. Summary (short version):

- Environment: model v3.1, sequence lengths 512 & 2048, batch=1 latency runs and batch=8 throughput runs using our harness. All runs on dedicated 80GB instances where applicable.

- A100 (full GPU):
  - TTFT (512): p50 52 ms, p95 110 ms
  - Throughput (tokens/sec single GPU): 4200 (batch=8)
  - Notes: predictable latency; MIG slicing (2x40GB) dropped throughput ~18% but improved density for small short-request workloads.

- H100 (full GPU):
  - TTFT (512): p50 48 ms, p95 100 ms
  - Throughput (tokens/sec single GPU): 5200 (batch=8)
  - Notes: best raw throughput and slightly better latency tail. MIG on H100 showed better isolation than A100 in our runs but takes some kernel/path tuning.

- L40S (full GPU):
  - TTFT (512): p50 70 ms, p95 160 ms
  - Throughput (tokens/sec single GPU): 3300 (batch=8)
  - Notes: good cost/perf for inference at scale but higher tail latency for long contexts. Limited MIG support; we recommend full GPU for L40S workloads.

Attached: bench-results-20270619.csv with raw metrics and per-request traces.

Sizing recommendation (initial):
- If target is latency-sensitive (p95 <= 120ms) and high throughput: H100 fleet with fallback A100 pool for cost control.
- For cost-sensitive high-density workloads: mixed L40S for stateless batching + A100 MIG for mixed short requests.

I’ll add the cost-per-token model once we get region pricing from procurement.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Performance Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Lucas Martin <lucas.martin@datapulse.com>, Procurement <procurement@datapulse.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Final MAP & close timeline — DataPulse evaluation sprint results

Lucas / Procurement team — thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on the bench results and the MAP draft, we’ve updated the MAP and included final recommendations. Deliverables attached: DP_MAP_v2.xlsx (final MAP) and bench-results-20270619.csv. Highlights:

- Evaluation outcome: H100 gives the best latency and throughput; A100 is a cost-effective fallback, and L40S is recommended where price-per-token is prioritized but higher tail latency is acceptable.
- Contract path: we propose a 6-month pilot on a mixed H100/A100 pool with a pricing collar. If pilot KPIs (TTFT/p95/throughput) are met, move to a 12-month reserved capacity contract.
- Timeline to close (proposed):
   - Week 0 (this week): procurement review + pricing alignment (Procurement)
   - Week 1: finalize SOW and pricing, DocuSign draft
   - Week 2–3: pilot provisioning & smoke tests
   - Week 4: pilot review and conversion decision

Next steps: Lucas, please confirm the model version you want pinned and Procurement — can you share region pricing constraints this week? I’ve linked the HubSpot deal (HS-4982) and a shared Drive folder with run artifacts.

Thanks — looking forward to closing quickly.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: DP_MAP_v2.xlsx, bench-results-20270619.csv
